answer: To keep a swarm from minting shadow voters, each newcomer must publish a work atlas whose tasks are assigned by three non-kin peers rather than self-chosen. Completions are sealed into a basalt registry that finalizes only after two full epochs, so cloned keys cannot flood cheap proofs. A rotating attestation beacon then probes one random coordinate on that map each epoch; a failed probe slashes the posted bond and freezes grading seats until the evidence is public. Maps that share motif hashes are merged as one operator.
